html: The single most striking result in the noise literature is about timing, not dose. Noise during the sleep phase causes the blood pressure rise, the endothelial dysfunction, the oxidative stress and the uncoupling of the synthase; the same noise during the waking phase does much less, and in the redox and endothelial readouts does nothing at all. The transcriptome of the exposed aorta points at two things: the circadian clock, dysregulated across aorta, heart and kidney, and FOXO3, down. This module draws what can be drawn of that. FOXO3 is the hub, and its switch is where it sits: the kinase AKT phosphorylates it, 14-3-3 binds the phosphorylated form and keeps it in the cytoplasm, and only the unphosphorylated factor reaches the nucleus. There it is read at two genes. One is the manganese superoxide dismutase, which is the canonical target and the reason the factor's loss is an antioxidant loss; the brain of a noise-exposed mouse also loses catalase message alongside the factor's own. The other is BMAL1, whose promoter carries a binding site for the factor, and that site is the one edge that makes the clock changes mechanism rather than a heat map: lose the factor and the positive limb of the clock loses a driver. The rest of the loop is drawn as it is known, CLOCK and BMAL1 together reading the period gene, the period-cryptochrome pair carried back into the nucleus to shut the dimer that made them. What is deliberately not drawn is an arrow from noise to any single clock gene. The individual genes come from sequencing with no direction stated and no perturbation, and inventing arrows from a heat map would be the easiest way to make this module look more certain than it is.
